lesson: Today we work on one technique. How a poem handles time. A poem can move through time or it can stop and hold on one moment. This one mostly holds still. It stays in a single morning, in one room before the day starts. Look at how it slows the moment down. You watch him from the window with one boot on, the other still cold in your hand. You are stuck between two actions, not moving yet. Then the hills won't hurry for anyone. Even the light is refusing to rush. The whole poem waits. That waiting works on you, because you feel the delay before action. You want the man to get up, and he doesn't yet. That builds a small pressure. Try this, freeze one moment right before something happens, and describe what is not moving. The second time through, listen for how the delay finally breaks at the end.
